subject: Request: SIG/SOC2 evidence — retention exception & sanitized postmortem
messages:
From: Alice Moore <alice.moore@fintrust.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: security-ops@fintrust.com
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: SOC2 / SIG inputs and telemetry window

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for taking time earlier. As part of FinTrust's SOC2 evidence intake for our Q4 audit, our security team needs the following from Redwood related to the authentication incident on 2026-08-12: 

- A brief, redacted postmortem (high-level timeline, root cause, mitigations) suitable for auditors (PII removed).
- A sanitized telemetry snapshot for the window 2026-07-12 — 2026-08-12 (we only need sampled logs and anonymized identifiers).
- Confirmation of Redwood's Incident Response Plan (IRP) version that was used and any deviations during this event.

Two constraints on our side: our compliance team cannot receive raw identifiers and we need an auditable transfer (SFTP or secure Drive link) with log retention metadata. We may also need a short memo that maps the provided artifacts to SIG+CAIQ control IDs (if possible).

Could you confirm whether Redwood can: 1) produce a sanitized telemetry snapshot, 2) provide a redacted postmortem, and 3) accommodate a temporary retention exception so we can review older audit logs that are normally archived after 90 days? If yes, what is the earliest you can deliver and how will you transmit?

Appreciate your help — we aim to close the evidence packet by 2026-08-25.

Best,
Alice Moore
Director, Security Assurance
FinTrust

Attachments: none
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Moore <alice.moore@fintrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T13:48:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: SOC2 / SIG inputs and telemetry window

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. We can support all three asks but need to coordinate a couple internal approvals and a short redaction pass. Proposed plan: 

1) Deliverables
   - Redacted postmortem PDF (high-level timeline, root cause, mitigations) — we will remove all customer identifiers and any session tokens.
   - Sanitized telemetry snapshot (sampled, hashed identifiers, schema map) compressed as .json.gz.
   - IRP extract (version + short deviation log) as a one-page summary.

2) Transfer method
   - We will stage artifacts to a one-time SFTP location and share ephemeral credentials. Link will include MD5 checksums and a short manifest.

3) Retention exception
   - We can temporarily rehydrate archive logs for the requested window and create a 14-day temporary retention exception for FinTrust reviewers. This requires approval from our Legal & Security ops (copied).

Tentative timeline: draft artifacts by 2026-08-18 EOD, final redacted bundle by 2026-08-20 after internal review. If that timeline works, we will proceed.

I'll loop in Marissa for the forensic artifacts and Jonas for retention approval.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Sr. Security Liaison
Redwood Inference

Attachments: IRP-summary-template.docx (stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-16T10:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: sanitized telemetry & retention exception — forensics snapshot and redaction notes

Sofia / Jonas — forwarding the initial packet from Forensics. I prepared a sanitized snapshot and a small evidence bundle; please see notes below before we send to FinTrust: 

- Contents (draft):
  * sanitized-telemetry-snapshot-20260815.json.gz — events hashed with salted HMAC, IPs bucketed to /24, user IDs replaced with UID-hash-X.
  * forensics-snapshot-20260815.tar.gz — timeline excerpts, anonymized request traces (internal use; not all included in public bundle).
  * redacted-postmortem-FT-20260815.pdf — contains timeline and mitigations, full PII/credential references redacted.

- Redaction checklist performed:
  1) Remove raw session tokens and request bodies that include user-entered text.
  2) Hash IDs with project salt and include salt ID mapping only in secure internal manifest.
  3) Strip any internal hostnames that map to customer-facing names.

- Retention exception ask: For FinTrust to validate sequence numbers against our archived logs, we need to rehydrate S3 Glacier segments for 2026-07-12 through 2026-08-12. Estimated rehydration time: ~6 hours; cost covered by Redwood (per standing audit support policy) but we need Jonas to approve the 14-day temporary retention exception and grant SFTP write tokens.

If approved, I will sanitize the final bundle and push to the ephemeral SFTP. Target to push the bundle 2026-08-18 morning.

—Marissa
Lead, Incident Forensics
Redwood Inference

Attachments: forensics-snapshot-20260815.tar.gz (43MB, stub)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Moore <alice.moore@fintrust.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T16:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: SOC2 / SIG inputs and telemetry window

Hi Alice — quick update from Redwood's ops/legal side: the retention exception is approved for a 14-day window scoped strictly to the files we discussed. We have provisioned a one-time SFTP path and generated ephemeral credentials (valid 48 hours). Delivery details below and next steps.

Delivery (secured):
- SFTP: sftp.redwood-inference.com (one-time path: /fintrust/onetime-20260818)
- Credentials: Ephemeral user and password were sent to Alice via separate secure channel.
- Files pushed: redacted-postmortem-FT-20260815.pdf, sanitized-telemetry-snapshot-20260815.json.gz, forensics-snapshot-20260815.tar.gz

Notes & mapping:
- We included a short mapping doc that links artifact sections to SIG control IDs (see manifest in the root of the SFTP).
- All files are redacted per our checklist; if you require further redaction, let us know and we'll iterate.

Next steps for FinTrust: please confirm receipt and whether the bundle satisfies the SIG/CAIQ mapping. If auditors need a short walkthrough, Marissa can run a 30-minute call to explain the telemetry schema and hash strategy.

Thanks — glad we could expedite this.

Jonas Weber
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
